In the figure above, $∠ABC$ is an angle and $D$ is a point in the interior of $∠ABC$ such that $m∠CBD=5x+{3}^{∘}.$ If $m∠ABC={106}^{∘}$ and $∠CBD≅∠ABD$, find the value of $x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14162998/assets/bdaee2dee98e41505c8a35c617a8f4fc035125ea8d504efecbe58afc9f7fd06c.png)

In the figure above,  $m \angle CBD = 5x - 5^\circ$ and $m \angle ABD =2x + 10^\circ .$ If $\angle CBD \cong \angle ABD$, find $m \angle ABC.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since $\angle CBD \cong \angle ABD$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠CBD & =m∠ABD \\ 5x-{5}^{∘} & =2x+{10}^{∘} \\ 5x & =2x+{15}^{∘} \\ 3x & ={15}^{∘} \\ x & ={5}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the measure of $\angle CBD$ is

$$
m \angle CBD = 5x - 5^\circ = 5 \cdot 5^\circ - 5^\circ = 20^\circ.
$$

So, by the angle addition postulate,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠ABC & =m∠CBD+m∠ABD \\  & =m∠CBD+m∠CBD \\  & =2\cdot m∠CBD \\  & =2\cdot {20}^{∘} \\  & ={40}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
